target_vertical: Cloud manufacturer / multi-channel D2C maker / light-mid manufacturing; food & beverage, apparel, cosmetics, electronics, furniture
pricing_model: Tiered subscription (Starter / Standard / Professional / Professional Plus / Enterprise) plus paid add-on modules (Manufacturing Management, Traceability, Warehouse Management, Insights, integrations). As of Feb 2026, Katana moved to a usage-based model tied to sales order line items / sales orders / GMV instead of revenue tiers; no per-user fees on most plans.
starting_price_usd: $299/month (Starter plan, billed annually) per katanamrp.com/pricing; effective monthly cost commonly $747-$1,095 once needed add-ons are stacked
free_trial_or_freemium: 14-day free trial; Free plan available limited to ~30 SKUs with core features
shopify_install_count: 136 reviews (Shopify App Store, Katana Cloud Inventory listing, as of early 2026)
shopify_sync_direction: Bi-directional. Products/variants/inventory: Katana to Shopify (Katana as system of record for stock). Orders: Shopify to Katana. Fulfillments/tracking: Katana to Shopify. Returns: Shopify to Katana (rolled out 2025).
shopify_synced_entities: Products, variants, inventory levels, sales orders, customers, fulfillments (with tracking), refunds/returns, service-type (non-physical) items. Draft orders [uncertain].
shopify_service_item_support: Yes — released 2025. Non-physical Shopify products (install, consulting, delivery) are imported as service items in Katana and can flow through Katana sales orders.
shopify_multi_store_support: Yes — multiple Shopify stores per Katana tenant; each can map to the same or different Katana locations (supports e.g. B2C and B2B stores under one tenant).
shopify_pos_support: Yes — Shopify POS supported with multi-sales-location mapping; each Shopify POS location can map to a distinct Katana location.
shopify_b2b_catalog_support: Partial — Katana supports B2B via a separate Shopify B2B store mapped to its own Katana location, and recommends SparkLayer for native Shopify B2B catalogs / company locations. Native handling of Shopify Plus B2B company / price-list objects: [uncertain]
shopify_variant_option_mapping: Variants matched by SKU; Katana improved SKU matching in 2025 for more robust mapping between Shopify variants and Katana variants. Each Shopify variant becomes a separate Katana variant linked to a parent product.
shopify_real_time_or_batch: Real-time / webhook-driven for orders and inventory updates; Katana states real-time sync of sales orders and inventory between Shopify and Katana, with 2025 reliability improvements for high-volume orders.
shopify_known_limitations: Common community complaints: pricing tied to sales-order volume / GMV can push low-AOV high-volume merchants into expensive tiers; some users report duplicated or mismatched SKUs requiring manual cleanup (pre-2025 improvements); historical/back-fill of old orders limited; multi-warehouse stock allocation can require careful location mapping; B2B price-list handling depends on third-party (SparkLayer).
etsy_supported: Third-party (via Extensiv Integration Manager and Make)
etsy_native_or_third_party: Third-party — primary path is via Extensiv Integration Manager (Cart Rover); also documented Make.com workflows. No direct Katana-built Etsy API connector.
etsy_listing_creation_vs_sync_only: Sync only — imports Etsy sales orders into Katana and pushes inventory levels back; not a listing creation tool.
etsy_inventory_sync: Inventory levels are pushed from Katana to Etsy via Extensiv. Frequency depends on Extensiv polling cadence (typically near real-time / minutes). [uncertain] exact interval.
etsy_order_import: Sales orders imported from Etsy via Extensiv automatically; near real-time depending on Extensiv polling.
etsy_synced_entities: Sales orders (with product and customer data), inventory levels, fulfillment status / tracking. Listings creation and personalization fields not supported.
etsy_known_limitations: Indirect (third-party) integration — adds Extensiv subscription cost and dependency. Tracking info must be added to the Katana sales order for fulfillment to sync back. Personalization fields and Etsy variations / digital products handling: [uncertain] / limited.
amazon_supported: Native (Amazon FBA via Katana-built SP-API integration since 2025) plus seller-fulfilled via Extensiv
amazon_marketplaces: Marketplaces across North America, Europe and Far East (each marketplace configured independently). Specific country list not enumerated publicly. [uncertain] full list
amazon_seller_types: FBA via native Katana SP-API integration; FBM / seller-fulfilled via Extensiv. Vendor Central: [uncertain] (not advertised).
amazon_synced_entities: Fulfillable inventory (real-time pull from Amazon), shipped FBA orders (imported as delivered sales orders with fulfillment records and stock movements), stock adjustments (auto-generated from reconciliation), SKU aliases per marketplace. Settlement reports, returns, customer messaging: [uncertain] / not in native FBA scope.
amazon_listing_creation: Sync only — Katana does not create or edit Amazon listings; SKUs are aliased and mapped to existing Amazon listings.
amazon_fba_inbound_workflow: [uncertain] — public docs describe FBA inventory sync and shipped-order import but do not explicitly document FBA inbound shipment creation flow within Katana.
amazon_settlement_report_handling: [uncertain] — not documented in public help articles; FBA financial postings appear to rely on Katana's standard sales-order-to-accounting flow (invoices to Xero/QBO) rather than ingesting Amazon settlement reports directly.
amazon_multi_account_support: Multiple Amazon marketplaces per tenant supported; multiple distinct Amazon seller accounts: [uncertain]
amazon_known_limitations: Settlement / financial reconciliation is not posted at marketplace-facilitator level (no native A2X-style summary). FBM relies on third-party Extensiv. Inbound FBA workflow not exposed natively. Some users report needing manual reconciliation between Amazon settlements and Katana-generated invoices in Xero/QBO.
xero_app_store_certified: Listed on Xero App Store (Katana Cloud Inventory). Certification badges: [uncertain]
xero_app_awards_recognition: Not listed among 2025 Xero Global App Award winners or published finalists
xero_synced_entities: Sales orders pushed as invoices, purchase orders pushed as bills, customers and suppliers imported from Xero, COGS journal entries (debit COGS / credit inventory) on delivered SOs, inventory balance journal. Payments and credit notes: [uncertain] / not primary scope.
xero_accounting_sync_mode: invoice_per_order — Katana pushes one invoice per sales order (and one bill per PO). Summary-journal / A2X-style summarized posting is not the default mode.
xero_cogs_journal_method: perpetual_per_movement — When an SO is moved to Delivered, Katana sends a journal entry debiting COGS and crediting Inventory, in line with invoicing (partial invoicing produces partial journals).
xero_multi_currency: Yes — supports multi-currency invoices/bills posting consistent with Xero multi-currency.
xero_tax_handling: Tax codes mapped from Xero — invoices pushed with applicable Xero tax codes; details of code mapping configurable per item / customer. [uncertain] full mapping rules.
xero_known_limitations: One-invoice-per-order can be noisy for high-volume D2C merchants vs A2X-style daily summaries; journal entries can be delayed up to ~10 minutes; sync errors on tax-code or account mapping require manual fix; customers must be unique by name to avoid duplicates.
qb_desktop_supported: No (QuickBooks Desktop is not supported natively; only QBO)
qb_app_certified: Listed on QuickBooks App Store; Intuit Developer Growth Program spotlight participant. Specific Intuit certifications: [uncertain]
qb_synced_entities: Invoices (from delivered SOs), bills (from POs), customers, vendors, COGS journal entries, inventory balance journal. Payments, credit memos: [uncertain] / not primary scope.
qb_accounting_sync_mode: invoice_per_order — one QBO invoice per Katana sales order; one bill per PO. Summary journal mode not the default.
qb_cogs_journal_method: perpetual_per_movement — on SO Delivered, Katana pushes a journal debiting COGS and crediting Inventory; partial invoicing creates proportional journals.
qb_multi_currency: Yes — multi-currency posting to QBO supported.
qb_known_limitations: QuickBooks Online only (no Desktop). One-invoice-per-order can generate large volumes for high-throughput D2C. Inventory must be managed in Katana, not QBO (Katana is system of record); duplicate customers/items in QBO require cleanup; serial/lot tracking is not reflected in QBO; up to ~10-minute delay on journals.
other_ecom_channels: Native: Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce. Via Extensiv Integration Manager / partners: Amazon (FBM), Etsy, eBay, Walmart, TikTok Shop (via Pipe17), Squarespace, Wix, Magento, Square, plus 100+ marketplace/cart connectors. Faire: [uncertain] (not listed natively).
bundle_kit_component_decomposition: Yes — BOMs and sub-assemblies decrement components when a parent sells / is produced; kits and configurable BOM products supported.
other_accounting_integrations: Native to Xero and QuickBooks Online only. Other accounting platforms (Sage 50/Intacct, MYOB, Zoho Books, FreshBooks, NetSuite, Wave): not native — integration only via API / Zapier / Make / iPaaS partners.
multi_level_bom: Yes — multi-level / nested BOMs with sub-assemblies (Manufacturing Management add-on / higher plans)
production_orders: Yes — Manufacturing Orders with operations / routings, shop-floor task assignments, scheduling and capacity planning; make-to-stock and make-to-order workflows.
batch_lot_tracking: Yes — batch / lot tracking with expiry, traceability for recalls (Traceability add-on / higher plans).
serial_tracking: Yes — serial number tracking on items / finished goods.
bin_location_support: Yes — storage bins / sub-locations within a warehouse, on Professional plan or higher (Warehouse Management add-on); supports zones, pick/pack stations.
multi_warehouse: Yes — Free / Standard up to 3 locations, Professional up to 10, Professional Plus unlimited.
barcoding: Yes — barcode generation, label support, and scanning via Shop Floor Control app (camera, USB or Bluetooth scanners); barcode-enabled receive / pick / pack / consume workflows.
purchase_orders: Yes — PO creation, partial receipts, supplier price lists, outsourced (subcontract) POs, multi-currency POs with supplier default currency.
supplier_management: Yes — supplier records with default currency, lead times, supplier-SKU mapping (purchase prices per supplier), MOQs [uncertain] explicit field.
landed_cost_support: Yes — additional costs (freight, duty, insurance) can be allocated to a PO and distributed by quantity or by value across line items, updating inventory cost.
multi_currency_inventory_valuation: Inventory valuation is held in the base currency; foreign-currency purchases are converted on receipt. (Single base currency for valuation.)
ai_demand_forecasting: Emerging — Katana announced AI embedding across planning, prediction and execution. Feb 2026 ConverSight integration delivers AI-powered BI / proactive insights on Katana inventory and sales data. Native built-in demand-forecasting ML model: [uncertain] in standard plans.
ai_purchase_order_suggestions: Reorder point and replenishment suggestions exist (replenishment management); explicit AI-generated PO drafts: [uncertain]
ai_natural_language_query: Yes (via ConverSight integration announced Feb 2026, which provides conversational BI over Katana data). Native in-app NL query: [uncertain]
public_api: Yes — public REST API documented at developer.katanamrp.com, with code samples in cURL, Node.js, Go, Ruby, Python; covers products, materials, BOMs, sales orders, manufacturing orders, purchase orders, inventory, customers, suppliers.
webhook_event_coverage: Outbound webhooks supported for key events (sales order created/updated/deleted and other entity changes). Full event list documented in Katana developer docs. [uncertain] exact coverage breadth.
integration_architecture: Mixed — native first-party integrations for Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Xero, QBO, Amazon FBA; iPaaS-based integrations (Extensiv Integration Manager, Make, Zapier) for Etsy, Amazon FBM, eBay, Walmart, TikTok, ShipStation, many 3PLs; plus open REST API for custom builds.
zapier_make_support: Yes — official Zapier app (8,000+ apps), official Make.com app, plus Extensiv Integration Manager.
mobile_app: Web-based Shop Floor Control app (floor.katanasfc.com) and Warehouse app accessible from any smart device browser; not distributed as a traditional native iOS / Android store app.
mobile_barcode_scanning_app: Yes — Shop Floor Control and Warehouse apps support camera-based barcode scanning on smartphones / tablets, plus USB and Bluetooth scanners.
rate_limit_handling_documented: [uncertain] — Katana publishes API docs but explicit public rate-limit and throttle documentation per integration (Shopify, Amazon, Xero, QBO) is not prominent.
sync_frequency: Shopify: real-time webhook-driven. Amazon FBA: real-time inventory pull plus daily/weekly reconciliation. Xero / QBO: near-real-time, journal entries can take up to ~10 minutes. WooCommerce / BigCommerce: real-time. Etsy and other Extensiv-routed channels: near-real-time (depends on Extensiv polling).
shipping_carrier_integrations: Direct: none built-in for label buying. Carriers reached via ShipStation (300+ carrier partnerships incl. USPS, UPS, FedEx, DHL), Easyship, Sendcloud, ClickShip; integration via Extensiv Integration Manager. No native carrier rate-shop / label-buy module inside Katana.
shipping_label_buying: Not native — requires ShipStation or similar third-party shipping platform.
three_pl_integrations: Via Extensiv (formerly 3PL Central / Cart Rover) ecosystem of 1,000+ 3PLs; ShipBob, ShipHero, Deliverr / Amazon MCF reachable through Extensiv or API; native 3PL connectors are limited.
edi_support: [uncertain] — not advertised as a native feature; typically achieved through partners / iPaaS.
g2_rating: [uncertain] exact star and review count; G2 listing exists for Katana Cloud Inventory with active reviews.
capterra_rating: [uncertain] exact star; Capterra listing active with reviews dated into Feb 2026.
notable_customers: Public case studies referenced by Katana include Brava Fabrics, Trew Knife Co., Pinpoint Laboratories, Vidaks (and others on katanamrp.com/customers). [uncertain] full list.
last_major_release: Feb 2026 — new pricing structure (usage-based, no per-user) plus ConverSight AI BI integration. 2025: Shopify service-item support, Shopify returns management, native Amazon FBA SP-API integration with real-time inventory and reconciliation, SKU-matching reliability improvements.
owner_parent_company: Independent — Katana SaaS OU, VC-backed; not owned by a larger ERP / e-commerce parent.
last_funding_event: Series B extension — €14M raised October 2025 (some sources report ~$16.4M Series B round Oct 2, 2025) led by Cogito Capital Partners, with participation from Northzone, Atomico, 42 Capital, Lightrock and Peter Fenton. Total funding ~$68.6M across 8 rounds.
public_status_page_uptime: [uncertain] — no widely promoted first-party status.katanamrp.com page. Third-party monitors (StatusGator, SaaSHub) track Katana availability.
